# apprentice

> apprentice is a free, open-source (MIT) macOS 14+ CLI and daemon in one Swift binary. It lets a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, opencode, Kilo, Cursor and others) or a hosted model use macOS, Linux and the web like a careful person: it reads one window as a numbered text list through the accessibility tree (no screenshots by default), acts with the real cursor and keyboard at a human pace, and proposes every change for approval.

apprentice is in beta: bug reports, playbooks for apps and sites, and fixes are welcome at https://github.com/robertsolves/apprentice/issues.

Use it at your own risk: it drives the Mac with the real cursor and keyboard, can make mistakes, and comes with no warranty; the user is responsible for what it does on their accounts. Playbooks are shared, so they must never hold personal information.

- Every change is a proposal first; risky steps (send, delete, buy, passwords, settings) go to the user in a small window or the chat.
- `apprentice phone` sets up push notifications in one tap (a private ntfy topic), so questions reach the user on their phone while they're away.
- Per-site budgets, cooldowns and allowlists; CAPTCHAs go to the user.
- Linux apps and browser sessions can run in a small Debian VM under Tart.
- Out of scope by design: bulk outreach, mass following, scraping at volume, several accounts on one site.
